newsitem.title: USA: Healthdyne seeks alternatives to Invacare bid.
newsitem.headline: Healthdyne seeks alternatives to Invacare bid.

text.p: Medical equipment maker Healthdyne Technologies Corp., trying to fight off a $200 million hostile takeover attempt by rival Invacare Corp., said Monday it was exploring alternatives to Invacare's latest bid.
Healthdyne said it would consider a merger or acquisition and was open to discuss such a possibility with third parties, including Invacare, if Invacare would withdraw its existing bid.

Invacare, whose existing bid was scheduled to expire last Friday, said it extended the bid until Aug. 1. Invacare launched the takever attempt in January with a bid of $12.50 a share and has since raised it three times, most recently to $15 a share.
Invacare said Monday that its existing stake, together with the shares stockholders had already agreed to tender, would give it more than 35 percent of Healthdyne's outstanding shares.
In a statement, Healthdyne said it was reaffirming its earlier decision not to sell or merge the company but was looking at alternatives.

"While the board has not made any decision to pursue any particular alternative, we believe it is prudent to talk with third parties to find out what the alternatives are," said Parker H. Petit, chairman.
Healthdyne's shares surged after the statement, trading at $17, up $1.50, on Nasdaq. Invacare was up 50 cents at $24 a share, also on Nasdaq.
When it raised its bid to $15 a share earlier this month, Invacare said it would not increase it further.
Healthdyne, based in Marietta, Ga., makes home health products for sleep disorders, breathing and infant monitors. It had sales of $118 million in 1996.
Invacare, based in Elyria, Ohio, makes wheel chairs, medical care beds, respiratory products and cardiovascular equipment and had sales of $610 million in 1996.
